sentences.text:
This is an application filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS),
2023.
2.
The petitioner is accused No.1 in Crime No.703/2025 of Kottyam West Police Station.
The offences alleged against the petitioner are punishable under Section 420 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. The prosecution case, as narrated in Annexure-A3 order, reads thus:
"In furtherance of their fraudulent and dishonest intention to make wrongful gain and cause corresponding wrongful loss to the informant.

the accused persons induced him to believe that they were the Branch Development Manager and the Managing Director of Southern Green Farming and Marketing Multi-State Co- operative Society Ltd., and by practicing deception, made him believe that if he deposited cash in the said society, he would be given interest at the rate of 12.5%.

entities.text: Southern Green Farming and Marketing Multi-State Co- operative Society Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As a result, the informant issued a cheque for Rs.4,00,000/-, drawn on his account maintained at SBI, Kodimatha Branch, in favour of the first accused for being deposited as an FD.

The accused paid interest at the rate of 12.5% till 27.10.2024, but on the maturity of the FD, they failed 2025:KER:84129 BAIL APPL. NO. 12086 OF 2025 to return the deposit amount and thereby cheated the informant, causing him a wrongful loss of Rs.4,00,000/- (sic)."

4. The case of the petitioner as discernible from Annexure A3 order, reads thus:
"3. The learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner was employed in the Ernakulam Branch of Southern Green Farming and Marketing Multi-State Co-operative Society Ltd. from 01.11.2022 to 31.10.2023, where one Anjali Jayaraj,
COURT O the niece of the informant, was as also working as Development Manager.

entities.text: Southern Green Farming and Marketing Multi-State Co-operative Society Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The said Anjali Jayaraj induced the informant to deposit money in the society for promoting its business and obtained incentives from the society.
The petitioner has not done anything to obtain the deposit from the informant.
The petitioner is innocent and he may be granted anticipatory bail.
(sic)."

5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Senior Public Prosecutor.
6.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has no involvement in the alleged misappropriation of funds by the Managing Director and the other office bearers of the Co-operative Society.

The 2025:KER:84129 BAIL APPL. NO. 12086 OF 2025 learned counsel submitted that being an employee, the petitioner was only discharging his duties by collecting deposits from the general public and depositing the same in various accounts.
The learned counsel submitted that, in a similar circumstance, this Court granted anticipatory bail to one of the employees of the Society referred to above (Annexure A4).
The learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that the petitioner is an employee of Ernakulam branch of the Society, whereas the alleged misappropriation occurred in Kottayam District.

2 7.

sentences.text: The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail plea.
The learned Public Prosecutor countered and submitted that the petitioner styled as Development Manger of the firm, approached various customers and collected money.
The learned Public Prosecutor further submitted that the further investigation in the matter will reveal whether the amount collected was deposited in the bank.

The learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the petitioner is the 2025:KER:84129 BAIL APPL. NO.
12086 OF 2025 accused in many other similar crimes.
The learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the petitioner, at the relevant time was working as the Development Manager of the firm in the Kottayam branch also.
Relying on the report submitted by the Investigating Officer, the learned Public Prosecutor contended that the custodial interrogation of the petitioner is required.
In Annexure A3 order, the learned Sessions Judge has noted that the petitioner is accused in similar cases registered at different police stations in the State.

8. As per Annexure A4 order, this Court granted bail to an employee of the firm in a different crime based on the finding that he had no role in disbursement of interest or return of principal amount.
9. Having regard to the circumstances brought out, this Court feels that the petitioner is not entitled to prearrest bail at this stage.
Therefore, the bail plea stands rejected.
2025:KER:84129 BAIL APPL. NO. 12086 OF 2025
However, the petitioner is granted one week time from this day to appear before the investigating officer for interrogation.

In the event, the petitioner is arrested by the Investigating Officer and upon production before the Jurisdictional Court, if he makes an application seeking regular bail, the learned Jurisdictional Court shall dispose of the application on the same day itself.
The Bail Application is disposed of as above.

Sd/-
